messages.subject: exiftool & imageRename function errors
parts:
Hello,
I am trying to work my way through vignette 1 but I cannot get the imageRename function to work. I get a warning for each one of my folders saying that the folder "contains no images; found 81 jpgs" and it says that for every folder. I'm trying to analyze camera trap data where each folder is one camera at a park. After all of the warnings for each folder, I also get an error saying "could not read DateTimeOriginal tag of any image. Check if the DateTimeOriginal tag is present in metadata with exifTagNames(). If not fixDateTimeOriginal() might help.
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In system(command.tmp, intern = TRUE) :
  running command 'exiftool -q -f -t -r -Directory -FileName -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal -ext JPG "c:/Users/Audrey/Desktop/Research Proposal/camtrapR/Station Folders/Carriage Hill CAT"' had status 65535"
Any function I use that involves the exiftool software I get the "status 65535" error but I don't know what that means. I can see the time and date stored in the data for each image when I go into the properties for the image so the metadata is there but the program isn't reading it. I've tried running R studio as an administrator and that didn't change anything. 

I'm working in R studio if that makes a difference. R is able to find the exiftool software (I'm assuming) based on the output for the Sys.which("exiftool"):
exiftool 
"C:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM32\\exiftool.exe"

Can someone please explain why I keep getting the status message, why R doesn't seem to register the images in the folders, and why my exiftool software isn't reading the metadata?
Thank you

Here is my code with the entire output: 

 #load in camtable
> parks_table <- read.csv("c:/Users/Audrey/Documents/RCodes/Metropark_Station_Table.csv", header = TRUE)
> #set working directory:

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: exiftool & imageRename function errors
parts:
Hi,
I haven't seen this problem before so I'm afraid I don't know how to fix it. When I google the error code 65535 the results indicate it is a file system error (e.g. here). 
Do you get the problem only with exiftool or with other software too?

Can you try running one of the exiftool calls directly in the command prompt (cmd.exe), e.g.:

That way we can make sure it has nothing to do with R. If the problem persists, try reinstalling exiftool. 
If that fails, try running the Windows system file checker tool to make sure the hard disk is ok. 

Alternatively, to make sure the code is ok, you could try running the same code on a different machine. 
I'm sorry I can't be more specific. It doesn't seem to be a camtrapR issue from what I can see. 
Let me know how it goes. 
Best,
Jürgen
